newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican peso closes stronger on U.S. treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Mexican peso closes stronger on U.S. treasuries.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed slightly stronger Friday as traders sold small amounts of dollar positions ahead of the weekend, after closely following dropping U.S. 30-year treasury bond yields, traders said.
"We thought that before the end of the trading day the peso could have been pressured due to end of the month (liquidity demand), but the market closely followed the long bond," a trader said.
Long bond yields were down to 6.75 percent, compared to 6.78 percent at the end of trading on Thursday.
The benchmark 48-hour peso gained 0.65 centavos to 7.9465/7.9490 to the dollar while its 24-hour stablemate gained 0.20 centavos to 7.9565/7.9590 to the dollar.
Same day contracts closed earlier 2.1 centavos stronger at 7.9330/7.9350 to the dollar.

Traders said that they expected the peso to lose ground against the dollar next week, due to the U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee meeting, the Mexican elections and the U.S. Fourth of July holiday.

"I think that next week the peso could fall under pressure due to the long weekend (in the U.S.) and the Mexican elections, but I don't think that it will go beyond 7.9800 (pesos per dollar)", another trader said.
